No server-side apply timestamp was captured and none is invented. DRY RUN observed 2026-08-17T01:01:11Z through 01:02:11Z, proposing 0183_client_budget_context.sql AND NOTHING ELSE, DRY-RUN EXIT 0. POST-APPLY VERIFICATION: migration list read 0183 | 0183. A full schema dump completed successfully (exit 0). WHAT IT SHIPS: public.client_budget_context — CURRENT practitioner-recorded budget context, one row per client (client_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so 'which budget is current' has no answer to get wrong). Chloe pilot feedback moved budget off treatment plans, where a client with several plans had several budget answers. Composite tenancy FKs to clients (id, studio_id) and practitioners (id, studio_id); studio_id derived by trigger from the parent client on every insert and update; updated_by_practitioner_id NOT NULL and VERIFIED at the database boundary against auth.uid()'s active practitioner in the row's own studio (0126's pattern in 0127's corrected, fully-qualified form); client_id and created_at immutable on UPDATE (rejected, not silently reset); created_at and updated_at forced server-side on INSERT because `default now()` is bypassed when a caller supplies the column. NO BACKFILL: treatment_plans.budget_notes is untouched, still exported, and rendered read-only as legacy plan history. ZERO BUSINESS-ROW MUTATION: 0183 is DDL plus GRANT/REVOKE only — no backfill, no INSERT, no UPDATE, no DELETE. The table is created empty. KNOWN DEFECT FOUND BY THE POST-APPLY SCHEMA DUMP, NOT YET REPAIRED IN PRODUCTION: 0183 stated its privilege contract as an allowlist ('authenticated gets SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE') but enforced it as a denylist (`revoke delete, truncate`). Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants the full set at create time, so every unnamed privilege survived. Production therefore reads GRANT SELECT,INSERT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER,MAINTAIN,UPDATE on public.client_budget_context TO authenticated, and the three new trigger functions carry EXECUTE to PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role. MAINTAIN is a PostgreSQL 17 privilege that no by-name revoke list written for 0183 could have contained. This is the same root cause recorded for 0129 (anon missed) and 0164 (service_role missed). MEASURED EXPLOITABILITY on a local database migrated to 0183: TRIGGER is EXERCISABLE — `create trigger ... on public.client_budget_context` SUCCEEDS as authenticated, because CREATE TRIGGER needs only table TRIGGER plus function EXECUTE and never ownership; MAINTAIN is exercisable (analyze runs); REFERENCES is granted but unreachable because CREATE on schema public is denied; the trigger functions are NOT callable as RPCs (PostgreSQL refuses a `returns trigger` function). 0184_client_budget_context_least_privilege.sql is AUTHORED AND TESTED to repair this and is NOT YET APPLIED. 0183 itself is FROZEN and was not edited.
